short: A polymath and philosopher who systematically laid the foundations for formal logic, biology, and the scientific method.
full:
Aristotle studied at Plato's Academy for twenty years before eventually founding his own school, the Lyceum, in Athens. His surviving writings read like lecture notes and cover an astonishing range of subjects, including physics, biology, zoology, metaphysics, logic, ethics, aesthetics, poetry, theatre, music, rhetoric, psychology, linguistics, economics, and politics.

He served as the tutor to a young Alexander the Great. His empirical approach to observing the natural world and his invention of formal logic dominated Western and Islamic intellectual history for over two millennia, making him one of the most influential scholars who ever lived.
